input.job: Post a weekly summary to a channel in the user's Slack workspace

guide.job: Post a weekly summary to a channel in the user's Slack workspace
guide.summary: Build a custom Slack app to manage OAuth authentication, configure necessary scopes for posting messages, and implement the authorization flow so users can connect their workspaces and allow your agent to post weekly summaries.

verdict.difficulty_reason: Requires registering a custom app, configuring OAuth scopes, implementing a callback route, managing token storage, and navigating workspace distribution requirements.
verdict.approval_wait: none for basic self-serve; workspace admin approval may be required depending on enterprise settings

paths.tradeoffs: Faster setup, but relies on Composio's managed authentication layer rather than your custom app.

steps.title: Create a new Slack app
actions: Go to the Slack API dashboard and click **Create New App**
Choose **From scratch**
Enter your app name and select your development workspace
steps.detail: Creating a custom app establishes the credentials and unique identifier required for OAuth communication with Slack.
steps.done_when: Your app is created and you are viewing its basic settings page.

steps.title: Configure OAuth redirect URLs
actions: Navigate to **OAuth & Permissions** in your app settings
Click **Add New Redirect URL**
Enter your callback URL and click **Add** then **Save URLs**
steps.detail: Setting up a valid redirect URL ensures Slack can securely return authorization codes back to your application during the sign-in flow.
steps.done_when: Your redirect URL is saved successfully in the OAuth settings.

steps.title: Add required bot token scopes
actions: In **OAuth & Permissions**, scroll to **Scopes**
Under **Bot Token Scopes**, click **Add an OAuth Scope**
Add chat:write and channels:read
steps.detail: Granting these specific scopes ensures your agent has permission to read channel information and post summary messages to invited channels.
steps.done_when: The required bot token scopes are listed under OAuth & Permissions.

steps.title: Extract client credentials
actions: Go to **Basic Information** in your app settings
Copy your **Client ID** and **Client Secret**
Store them securely in your environment variables
steps.detail: Your agent needs the Client ID and Client Secret to initiate the OAuth flow and exchange authorization codes for access tokens.
steps.done_when: Client ID and Client Secret are saved in your local environment file.

steps.title: Implement OAuth sign-in flow in code
actions: Build an auth route redirecting users to Slack's authorization URL
Build a callback route handling the code exchange for tokens
Store the returned access token securely against the user record
steps.detail: Writing the backend OAuth handler enables external users to log in with their Slack credentials and grant access to your application.
steps.agent_prompt: Write an Express.js route /auth/slack that redirects the user to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with client_id and scopes chat:write,channels:read. Also write /auth/slack/callback to exchange the code for a token using POST https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access.
steps.done_when: Your server successfully exchanges an authorization code for a valid Slack access token.

steps.title: Implement weekly summary posting action
actions: Write code to call chat.postMessage using the stored user token
Format the weekly summary payload with text and target channel ID
Schedule or trigger the function to execute weekly
steps.detail: Using the acquired token, your agent can now call the Slack Web API to publish weekly updates directly into the designated channel.
steps.agent_prompt: Write a function postWeeklySummary(token, channelId, message) that calls Slack's POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage using Bearer authentication with the provided token.
steps.done_when: The agent function successfully compiles and is ready for integration testing.

steps.title: Test OAuth and posting end-to-end
actions: Start your local server and trigger the sign-in flow
Authorize the app in your test Slack workspace
Invoke the agent function to post a test summary message
steps.detail: End-to-end testing verifies that the complete lifecycle from user sign-in to posting messages functions seamlessly without errors.
steps.done_when: A test message appears in your target Slack channel via your agent code.

steps.title: Make your agent do the job
actions: Copy the prompt below into your coding agent.
Run it once with your own account.
steps.detail: This is the point of the prototype: your agent using the connection.
steps.done_when: Your agent completed the job in Slack for your own account.
steps.agent_prompt: First check the connect step really happened: the Slack tool exists and is registered with my agent.  If anything is missing, stop and tell me what. Otherwise run my agent once on this job with my own account: Post a weekly summary to a channel in the user's Slack workspace. Show me what changed in Slack.

dimensions.note: Uses OAuth 2.0 for connecting workspaces securely.
Self-serve app registration available via the Slack API portal.
None for personal accounts or public distribution activation (checklist only); optional Slack Marketplace listing requires review and 10+ installed workspaces.
Public distribution requires the Activate Public Distribution button, while workspace admins can block or require approval for installs.
Agents connect to individual user workspaces.
Workspace admins may block installs or require approval depending on company security policies.
OAuth tokens must be securely stored and refreshed.
Narrow scopes limit posting to invited channels, while broader scopes allow posting to public channels without an invite.
Tests are typically run directly within a designated development workspace.
The agent posts on a schedule and does not require an incoming app event to start.

decisions.title: Who will connect their account?
decisions.why_it_matters: Other people signing in can mean an approval wait.

options.label: My users
options.what_it_means: Other people connect their own accounts to your agent.
options.recommended_reason: You're building for other people, so the guide covers what it takes to launch.

options.label: Just me
options.what_it_means: Only your own account, to try the idea first.

decisions.title: How will your agent connect to this app?
decisions.why_it_matters: Choose how your agent signs in and manages Slack connections for users.

options.label: Use Composio
options.what_it_means: Composio handles sign-in, token refreshes, and provides ready-made Slack actions.
options.recommended_reason: It gives you immediate access to ready-made actions and managed sign-in without building custom OAuth handling.

options.label: Use your own app
options.what_it_means: You register a custom Slack app, handle sign-in, and store tokens yourself.

decisions.title: Whose name should users see at sign-in?
decisions.why_it_matters: Your own name means your own approval.

options.label: Composio's name
options.what_it_means: Users sign in through Composio's Slack app, already approved.
options.recommended_reason: It skips registering and reviewing your own app. You can switch to your own later.

options.label: Your own app
options.what_it_means: Register your own Slack app and plug it into Composio.

decisions.title: What permissions does your agent need?
decisions.why_it_matters: Control where the agent can post messages in user workspaces.

options.label: Post to invited channels
options.what_it_means: The agent can only post messages to channels where the bot has been explicitly added.
options.recommended_reason: Provides a safer permission boundary by restricting the agent to channels it was explicitly invited to.

options.label: Post to any channel
options.what_it_means: The agent can post to any public channel without needing an invitation.

library.challenge: Distributing to other workspaces; admins can restrict apps.
